prompt: Tower A has $2$ blocks on day $1$ and grows by $3$ blocks each day. Tower B has $4$ blocks on day $1$ and grows by $6$ blocks each day. On day $7$, how many MORE blocks does Tower B have than Tower A?
hint: Day $1$ is the starting day for both towers. Think about how many times each tower grows before day $7$ arrives.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Find day $3$ first. Tower A: $2, 5, 8$. Tower B: $4, 10, 16$. The gap is $16 - 8 = 8$. Day $7$ works exactly the same way, just with more steps.
Day $1$ is the starting day for both towers. Think about how many times each tower grows before day $7$ arrives.
Both towers grow $6$ times. Tower A has $2 + 6 \times 3$ blocks and Tower B has $4 + 6 \times 6$ blocks. Find both, then subtract.
Tower A has $20$ blocks and Tower B has $40$ blocks, so Tower B has $40 - 20 = 20$ more blocks.

explanation: Day $1$ is the start, so reaching day $7$ means each tower grows $6$ times, not $7$.
Tower A on day $7$ has $2 + 6 \times 3 = 2 + 18 = 20$ blocks in all.
Tower B on day $7$ has $4 + 6 \times 6 = 4 + 36 = 40$ blocks in all.
The difference is $40 - 20 = 20$, so Tower B has $20$ more blocks.

alternativeExplanations.title: Write both patterns out
steps: On the seventh entry, $40 - 20 = 20$ blocks apart.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The most common wrong answer is $23$: it comes from adding the daily growth $7$ times ($2 + 7 \times 3 = 23$ and $4 + 7 \times 6 = 46$, gap $23$).
But day $1$ is the starting pile — no blocks have been added yet on day $1$.
Escape it by writing the first three days out by hand before you multiply; you will see the number of ADDITIONS is always one less than the day number.
